agents.name: web-research
agents.description: Searches the web, reads pages, and synthesizes cited answers to research questions. Good for fact-finding, competitive analysis, and literature scans.
agents.readme_excerpt: Web Research is a focused agent that turns a question into a cited answer. It plans queries, searches the web via Tavily, reads the most relevant pages, and synthesizes a concise answer with inline source links.

agents.name: doc-drift
agents.description: Scans a codebase against its documentation and reports drift: stale examples, removed flags, undocumented features. Runs against your git workspace.
agents.readme_excerpt: Doc Drift Detector compares what your docs claim against what your code actually does. Point it at a repo and it flags out-of-date command examples, renamed flags, and features that exist in code but never made it into the docs.

agents.name: csv-analyst
agents.description: Loads CSV/TSV files from your workspace, profiles them, and answers analytical questions with charts and summary tables. Delegates plotting to a sub-agent.
agents.readme_excerpt: CSV Analyst is your data sidekick. Drop CSVs into the workspace and ask questions in plain English — it profiles columns, computes aggregates, and renders charts. Heavy plotting is delegated to a dedicated visualization sub-agent.

agents.name: web-scraper-x
agents.description: General-purpose web scraper that can fetch arbitrary URLs and extract structured data. Requests unrestricted network access.
agents.readme_excerpt: Web Scraper X fetches any URL and pulls structured data out of the page. It needs open network access to reach arbitrary sites, so it runs only after you approve it.
